Measured 2026-10-22: 37.95 km2, the World Bank's exclave polygon 38.07 km2. Artsvashen (O04) is given back to Gadabay District (AZ-GAD): Azerbaijan has held it since 1992 (wiki:en:6251782@1377070396; web:3355000f23357472, Armenpress, 9 July 2026: it 'remains under Azerbaijan's control'). Overture 2026-08-19.0 drew it in AZ-GAD; release 2026-09-23.1 draws it as a detached part of Armenia's AM-GR and in no Azerbaijani region. Fill follows the ground (ruled 2026-10-08 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj)); accepted 2026-10-22 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj). Once Overture draws it in AZ-GAD again, the row is withdrawn.

Tiris Zemmour's north-west corner, about 326 km2 at 12.00-11.67 W, 25.75-26.00 N, belongs to MR-11. Overture 2026-08-19.0 drew it in MR-11; release 2026-09-23.1 redrew the region (division_area c634584a-897a-40eb-bd92-962925d94cf8, version 5 to 6) without it, leaving it in Mauritania's country land but in no region; the World Bank's version 3 puts it in Tiris Zemmour (admin 1 MRT012). Measured 2026-10-27: the only piece of Mauritania's land over 2 km2 in no region in either release; the other 12 km2, 38 coastal slivers both releases share, lie in the sea by the World Bank's line and are left alone. Ruled 2026-10-27 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj). Once Overture draws the corner in MR-11 again, the row is withdrawn.

Isla de Perejil (GeoNames 2538499, an island) is cut out of Overture's Ceuta (ES-CE): disputed_areas.tsv (B62) holds it for nobody, kept deserted under the 2002 status quo and claimed by Spain and Morocco, and at 0.14 km2 it is under the size floor for drawing a disputed area, so Ceuta's card drew and ringed it as Ceuta's own land. Measured 2026-11-12 on Overture 2026-09-23.1: two parts within 1,000 m of the point, the island (0.1416 km2) and a rock 399 m west (0.0003 km2); Ceuta's own land lies 3.4 km away and more. Ruled 2026-11-12 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj). If Overture drops the island, the row is withdrawn.

Bhutan's card is drawn from the World Bank's outline, which leaves Doklam (its Non-Determined Legal Status Area, 596 km2) to nobody and the northern valleys (B75, held by Bhutan, claimed by China) to China, so the card drew Doklam white and the valleys grey. Natural Earth draws both in Bhutan, and disputed_areas.tsv has Bhutan holding B75 and B76, so Natural Earth's ground there is given back. Guard points: Sharithang, GeoNames 1252449, in the Doklam area; Lunana, GeoNames 1337390 (Gasa), in B75. Measured 2026-11-18 over every country card drawn from another dataset: only Bhutan has such ground (Mayotte's and South Georgia's gaps are coastline differences inside whole-card areas, left alone). Ruled 2026-11-18 by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj).

Oecusse's EEZ zone, which Marine Regions keys to no card of its own, is tinted on Oecusse's card (TL-OE) as well as on Timor-Leste's. The zone is found by geometry, never by the sovereign field: the zone whose island is a part of the card's land at least 90% within 30 km of the zone. It is the one listed exception to the rule that a subdivision draws its nation's whole waters or none, ruled with the rule that an island's zone is tinted on its sovereign's card only where the island is on the main map or in the detail panel (2026-10-13 and 2026-10-16, by Jens Nordmark (@nordmarj)).
